$comment: The Chief thread's structure, machine-readable (cmuxterm-hq docs/design/chief-thread.md is the prose). tests/ui-structure/thread_structure.py checks a thread snapshot against it. Geometry is in points, from the accessibility tree, so it holds whichever renderer draws the thread (the native transcript, a web page). Numbers come from the native transcript at b7d534e^, before #37736 and #37777 (Packages/Shared/CmuxMessagesLab Vendor/catalyst/Fixture.swift and Layout.swift Metrics), which matches macOS Messages.

chief-panel.$comment: The Chief panel: one conversation, no list column.

conversation-tab.$comment: A conversation tab: one conversation, no list column.

home.$comment: The docked Home Messages view: the list column on the left is allowed; the thread right of it obeys every other rule.

thread.$comment: The thread is one accessibility container named Messages (an AXList natively, a labelled region or log on the web). Its messages are its elements with role description 'message' (title: the sender, 'You' for mine) or, on the web, the bubble groups inside it.

bubble.$comment: Text column: 358.4 pt at a 628 pt thread, plus 0.654 pt per point of width (below 434 pt it keeps its 434 pt share). A bubble is the column plus 12 pt of padding each side.

alignment.$comment: Mine hug the right edge (20 pt side, 6 pt tail); others the left, after the 36 pt avatar column in a group.

avatar.$comment: An avatar sits inside the thread, beside the last bubble of an incoming run: bottom-aligned with it, just left of it.

attachment.$comment: Inline at bubble size: never wider than a link preview (350 pt), never wider than the bubble column.

needs_you.$comment: A Needs you item is one inline card or bubble in the thread, said once; the same item never repeats as the heading of several cards.

rules.says: The surface has one thread container named Messages.
A single-conversation surface's thread spans it edge to edge: no list or avatar column beside it.
Every avatar sits inside the thread, bottom-aligned with an incoming bubble and just left of it.
No bubble is wider than the bubble column for the thread's width.
No message is a full-width card.
Mine hug the right edge, others the left.
Attachments are inline, inside the thread, at bubble size.
A Needs you item shows once, inline, not as a repeated heading.
Where tails are reported, the last bubble of each run has one and no other bubble does.
